mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower borrowing costs and economic support.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS over 20-day returns falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or average 20-day returns during declining FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly positive (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts decline below 1500.0 thousand units signals weakening residential demand, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and business investment confidence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1500.0, or Rank IC for HOUST < 1500.0 is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 and housing starts (HOUST) below 1500.0 signals broad-based economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings growth and recession risk.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0 and HOUST < 1500.0, or Rank IC for joint condition is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, a rising unemployment rate above 4.5% signals labor market weakness, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate slowing economic growth and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances during late-cycle expansions when UNRATE > 4.5%, or Rank IC for UNRATE in late-cycle is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate above 2.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced equity valuations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5, or Rank IC for CPIAUCSL > 2.5 is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates and business investment increases.
failure_condition: Rank IC for RSAFS over 20-day returns falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or average 20-day returns during rising RSAFS periods are not significantly positive (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a federal funds rate above 5.0% signals aggressive rate hikes, which typically cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate investment and consumer spending pressures.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances during monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or Rank IC for FEDFUNDS in tightening cycles is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payroll employment below 137000.0 thousand and rising unemployment rate above 4.5% signals labor market deterioration, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS < 137000.0 and UNRATE > 4.5, or Rank IC for joint condition is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.
